title: People are claiming AI trading bots can turn €80 into €5,000. Is this the future of trading or just another massive scam?
author: jorguice
selftext:
I’ve been getting increasingly curious about AI trading bots lately, and I genuinely want to hear the opinions of people who actually have experience with them.  
For some context, I have a basic understanding of trading concepts like stop losses, average entry prices, liquidity, and a few other fundamentals. However, I wouldn’t consider myself an experienced trader, since I’ve never seriously dedicated much time to active trading.  
I’ve mainly been a crypto holder throughout this market cycle. I bought Solana at around $80 and Bitcoin at approximately $60,000, intending to hold them rather than actively trade.  
But recently, something has really caught my attention.  
**I keep seeing videos claiming that AI-powered trading bots can turn ridiculously small amounts of money, like €80, into €5,000 in profits.**  
Some people are even claiming that these bots will eventually make traditional, manual trading obsolete because AI can analyze markets, identify opportunities, and execute trades faster than humans.  
I’ve also come across people selling these so-called AI trading bots for around €500.  
And honestly, I don’t know what to believe.  
Part of me thinks that if these bots were genuinely capable of generating such insane returns, why would anyone sell them for a few hundred euros instead of simply using them to make money themselves?  
On the other hand, AI technology is developing incredibly fast, so I’m curious whether there’s actually something legitimate behind all this hype.  
**So I have a few genuine questions for people who know more about this than I do:**  
Are AI trading bots actually profitable, or are most of the ones being advertised online scams?  
Has anyone here personally used one and achieved consistent, verifiable profits?  
Are legitimate AI trading bots accessible to ordinary retail traders, or are the effective ones mostly private or institutional?  
Can you actually buy a reliable trading bot, or would you need to develop your own?  
Do you think AI could eventually outperform most human retail traders and fundamentally change the trading industry?  
I’m not expecting some magical money-printing machine, and I understand that trading always involves risk.  
I’m just genuinely curious about how much of this is real technology and how much is clever marketing designed to attract inexperienced people.  
**I’d especially appreciate hearing from people who’ve actually tested these bots with real money, including those who lost money using them.**  
Is AI trading really the future, or are people just falling for another expensive crypto scam?

comments.author: TrenchersAi
comments.body:
Anyone promising €80 to €5,000 is selling you something, usually the bot itself or a "managed account" where you send them money. Real bots don't come with guaranteed returns, because no strategy has them.

What a bot actually does is follow rules faster and more consistently than you can. Buy when X happens, sell at Y, never risk more than Z per trade. If the rules are bad, it just loses money faster.

Some quick red flags:  
\- They need you to deposit funds with them instead of keeping your own wallet or account  
\- Screenshots of returns but no verifiable history  
\- Pressure to join now, or referral bonuses for bringing in friends  
\- They won't explain what the strategy actually does

If you're curious, the safer way to learn is a bot that runs on paper or demo money first, so you can watch how it behaves without losing anything. Most people find out pretty quickly that the hard part is the rules, not the automation.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Your instinct about "if it worked, why sell it for €500" is a good one, and the fixed-return claims in those videos are a warning sign by themselves. I can't speak to anyone's personal results, but I'd ask any seller for a long record that includes the losing trades, the fees, and the worst drop. I'd also never share an API key that can withdraw, and I'd test with paper money before risking real money. Cymetica lets you run an AI agent in paper mode on a practice balance, so you can see how a bot behaves without spending anything.
